title: Displacement, velocity and acceleration

draft.title: Displacement, velocity and acceleration
card: For a particle moving in a straight line, x(t) is its displacement from the origin at time t. Velocity is v = dx/dt and acceleration is a = dv/dt.
Going the other way, integrate. Velocity is the integral of acceleration, and displacement is the integral of velocity. Each integral adds a constant C.
An initial condition fixes the constant. Put in the given values of t and v (or x), then solve for C.
If a = 6t and v = 2 when t = 0, then v = 3t² + C. Putting in t = 0 gives 2 = C, so v = 3t² + 2. At t = 1, v = 5.
draft.remember: Differentiate to go from x to v to a. Integrate to go back, and use the starting values to find C.

a.q: A particle has displacement x = t³ − 4t metres at time t seconds. What is its velocity when t = 2?
a.why: v = dx/dt = 3t² − 4, so at t = 2, v = 12 − 4 = 8 m/s. The value 0 is x itself at t = 2 (8 − 8), which is displacement, not velocity.
a.clue: Differentiate x first, then put in t = 2.

b.q: A particle has acceleration a = 4t m/s². When t = 0 its velocity is 3 m/s. What is its velocity when t = 2?
b.why: Integrating gives v = 2t² + C. Since v = 3 when t = 0, C = 3, so v = 2t² + 3. At t = 2, v = 8 + 3 = 11 m/s. The answer 8 comes from leaving out the constant.
b.clue: Integrate a, then use v = 3 at t = 0 to find C before putting in t = 2.
